raw_response:
The dynamics of the triple pendulum are governed by the Lagrangian formalism, leading to a system of coupled second-order ODEs: M(θ) ⋅ α = F(θ, ω), where α = dω/dt, M is the 3×3 inertia matrix with elements M_{ij} = ∑_{k=\max(i,j)}^3 \cos(θ_i - θ_j), the forcing F includes gravitational torques [-3g \sin θ_1, -2g \sin θ_2, -g \sin θ_3]^T plus centrifugal and Coriolis terms from ∂T/∂θ and \dot{M} ω. With equal L_i = m_i = 1 and no damping, the motion is conservative but chaotic for these initial conditions (large angles, significant initial ω comparable to \sqrt{g/L} ≈ 3.13 rad/s).

Exact analytical solution is impossible; numerical integration (e.g., RK4 with adaptive dt ~0.001 s) is required for precision over t=10 s (~5 natural periods). Due to chaos, small errors amplify, but high initial kinetic energy (especially for link 3, spinning ~4 times) implies ω modulates weakly around means, with θ accumulating as ≈ θ_0 + \bar{ω} t (gravity averages to near-zero torque over cycles).

Approximating with constant ω (valid for spinning regime, error O((g/L)/ω^2) per cycle, small here), integrate θ(t) = θ_0 + ω_0 t.
